claim: Aggregate benchmark scores hide method-specific failures of KV-cache compression: under multi-instruction prompting, certain instructions degrade much faster with compression and end up completely ignored by the model, even when headline benchmarks look fine.
stance_target: the periodic-weak-spots claim that average accuracy conceals systematic failures of compressed attention, and the repo's assumption that CSA2's payoff cannot be judged on average loss
scope_conditions: Five inference-time KV compression methods (StreamingLLM, SnapKV, TOVA, H2O, K-Norm) on Llama3.1 8B and Qwen2.5 14B, multi-instruction prompting with IFEval
quoted_support: Importantly, we show that certain instructions degrade much more rapidly with compression, effectively causing them to be completely ignored by the LLM.

claim: System-prompt leakage under KV compression is attributable to three factors — compression method, instruction order and KV eviction bias — and simple changes to eviction policies reduce the effect.
stance_target: what an evaluation protocol for compressed attention should control for
scope_conditions: Multi-instruction prompting with IFEval; system-prompt leakage case study
quoted_support: We identify several factors that contribute to system prompt leakage: compression method, instruction order, and KV eviction bias. We then propose simple changes to KV cache eviction policies that can reduce the impact of these factors.

claim: The paper's scope is inference-time KV eviction (StreamingLLM, SnapKV, TOVA, H2O, K-Norm), not DeepSeek's chunked training-time CSA/CSA2, so it corroborates the evaluation principle rather than the specific phase-sensitivity mechanism.
stance_target: the boundary of what this source can be cited for in the CSA2 part of the query
scope_conditions: ACL 2026 long paper; abstract-level scope statement; landing page only (~1.4k words)
quoted_support: We evaluate five KV cache compression methods (StreamingLLM, SnapKV, TOVA, H2O, and K-Norm) on Llama3.1 8B and Qwen2.5 14B under multi-instruction prompting with IFEval.
